The full suite is green. 

I implemented the disposable-domain blocklist as a dedicated pipeline step, keeping each piece of logic in its own single-responsibility unit and following the existing OfficeFloor conventions:

1. **`ValidateEmailDomain`** — a new validation step that reads the shared `@Val OwnerFieldsDto`, extracts the domain, and throws when it matches the blocklist (`mailinator.com`, `tempmail.com`, `guerrillamail.com`). It sits right after `NormalizeOwnerEmail`, so it works on the already-syntax-validated, lower-cased address and skips the optional/blank case — no duplication of the email-syntax logic.

2. **`DisposableEmailDomainException`** — a checked exception mirroring the existing `InvalidEmailException`.

3. **`DisposableEmailDomainExceptionHandler`** + its escalation YAML — responds 400 with a `ProblemDetail` (reusing the shared `ProblemDetails.build` helper) carrying the rejected value.

4. **`owners.POST.yml`** — wired the new `validateEmailDomain` step into the pipeline between `normalizeEmail` and `ensureUniqueIdentity`, under the same `transaction` governance as its neighbors.

The `errorRejectsDisposableDomain` acceptance test and the entire existing suite pass.
